summary: This CSS rule truncates paragraph text to exactly three lines and adds an ellipsis (…) at the end. It uses a combination of modern and older browser-specific properties to ensure the truncation works across different browsers, and sets a max-height to enforce the three-line limit.

explanations.2: display: -webkit-box enables the flexbox layout model specifically for older WebKit browsers (Safari, Chrome) so we can use line-clamping on them.
explanations.3: -webkit-line-clamp: 3 is the WebKit-specific property that actually limits the text to 3 lines; the standard line-clamp on line 4 does the same for modern browsers.
explanations.5: -webkit-box-orient: vertical tells the webkit flexbox to arrange items vertically (top to bottom) rather than horizontally, which is required for line-clamping to work.
explanations.7: text-overflow: ellipsis adds the three dots (…) at the end when text gets cut off, so users know there's more content.
explanations.10: max-height calculates the physical height: 3 lines × 1.5em per line = 4.5em total, which gives the browser a hard pixel limit to respect.
explanations.11: line-height: 1.5em sets the height of each line of text to 1.5em, which is used in the max-height calculation above.
